<p class="print-note">Eight analysts, each overclaiming in a different way.
Cut along the dashed lines, deal one per team. Page&nbsp;2 is the critique
sheet.</p>

<div class="sheetwrap">
<div class="cards">

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 1</span>
    <h3>Complaints per store</h3>
    <p class="setup">Outcome: number of complaints per store per month. Mostly 0, 1 or 2; a few stores hit 15. Estimated by OLS.</p>
    <p class="claim">"Adding one staff member cuts complaints by 0.4 per month. At our smallest stores that takes us below zero."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Is the model wrong, or only the sentence?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 2</span>
    <h3>The 0.03% lift</h3>
    <p class="setup">2.4 million users, randomised. Effect on conversion: +0.03 percentage points, p &lt; 0.001.</p>
    <p class="claim">"Highly significant. Roll it out to everyone."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Significant of what?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 3</span>
    <h3>The pilot that "failed"</h3>
    <p class="setup">38 stores. Estimated effect +12%, 95% interval from −4% to +28%, p = 0.14.</p>
    <p class="claim">"No significant effect. Kill the programme."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> What has actually been shown?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 4</span>
    <h3>The elasticity</h3>
    <p class="setup">Three years of the firm's own transaction data. Its price changed twice in that period, both times by about 2%.</p>
    <p class="claim">"We estimate demand is inelastic, so we can raise prices."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> What did the standard error have to work with?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 5</span>
    <h3>The 112% customer</h3>
    <p class="setup">Outcome: churn, coded 0 or 1. Fitted with a linear model on tenure, spend and support tickets.</p>
    <p class="claim">"This customer has a 112% probability of churning, so prioritise them."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Name the specific problem.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 6</span>
    <h3>The log coefficient</h3>
    <p class="setup">Outcome: log of units sold. Coefficient on price: −1.8, standard error 0.3.</p>
    <p class="claim">"Raising price by one dollar costs us 1.8 units."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Read it back in the units of the problem.</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 7</span>
    <h3>R² of 0.94</h3>
    <p class="setup">Weekly sales regressed on advertising spend, same market, three years. R² = 0.94.</p>
    <p class="claim">"The model explains 94% of sales. Doubling ad spend will roughly double them."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Which question does this model answer?</p>
  </div>

  <div class="card">
    <span class="n">Card 8</span>
    <h3>The 97%</h3>
    <p class="setup">A single estimate, p = 0.03.</p>
    <p class="claim">"There is a 97% chance the effect is real, so we can act on it."</p>
    <p class="ask"><b>Critique.</b> Say precisely what p = 0.03 does mean.</p>
  </div>

</div>

<div class="pagebreak"></div>

<div class="defence">
  <h3>Critique sheet — team <span style="color:#b31b1b">______</span> &nbsp;·&nbsp; card <span style="color:#b31b1b">____</span></h3>

  <p class="vocab">Name it: <b>wrong model for the shape of the outcome</b> ·
  <b>significant ≠ large</b> · <b>not significant ≠ no effect</b> ·
  <b>not enough variation in X</b> · <b>predictions outside the possible range</b> ·
  <b>coefficient read in the wrong units</b> · <b>fit is not a causal claim</b> ·
  <b>that is not what a p-value says</b></p>

  <p class="lbl">What they are actually entitled to claim</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">Where exactly the sentence goes wrong</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">What would you need to see before you believed it?</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">Is our own project at risk of this same error? How would we know?</p>
  <div class="row"></div>

  <p class="lbl">From the floor: the objection that landed</p>
  <div class="row"></div>
</div>
